Table~\ref{tab:simulators} prints, for each engine, the contact formulation it names, whether it exposes interpenetration depth and how many first-party hand models it ships; its empty-cell count is over the seven property columns. \emph{contact model} and \emph{solver} are controlled vocabularies: \emph{soft} for a compliant or regularised contact, \emph{convex relaxation} for a convexified formulation, \emph{complementarity} for an LCP, \emph{hard NCP} for a nonlinear complementarity problem, \emph{impulse} for a velocity-level update, and \emph{rigid, model unstated} where the source describes collision geometry but names no contact law. The sentence each was read from runs to several hundred characters; \texttt{corpus/rows/} carries each one verbatim, because Section~IV's argument turns on its wording. \emph{penetration exposed} is whether the engine makes interpenetration depth readable by a user's code without patching it. \emph{hands} counts first-party hand models in the parsed snapshot, and they are: \emph{Brax} synthetic 4-fingered claw hand; \emph{Genesis} Shadow Hand; \emph{Isaac Gym} Shadow Dexterous Hand, Allegro Hand, TriFinger; \emph{Isaac Lab} KUKA Allegro hand, ShadowHand, AbilityHand, Fourier GR1-T2 dex hands, Unitree Inspire hand, Unitree trihand; \emph{ManiSkill3} Allegro Hand, Ability Hand, Inspire Hand, Delto 3-finger hand, TriFinger; \emph{Newton} Allegro Hand; \emph{Orbit} Allegro hand.
